# Lock Jelly WebGPU Canal Diorama ![Preview by @vib3coded](<../data/gifs/2110329593441796383.gif>) By [@vib3coded]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — single self-contained HTML file: Specify one HTML deliverable for easy browser playback; still check whether the implementation loads external dependencies. ## Prompt (English) ```text Build "Lock Jelly." — a single self-contained HTML file (WebGPU + WGSL, no libraries, no network, works from file://), part of a "Material Studies" series of jelly dioramas. If WebGPU is missing or the adapter fails, show a clean fallback card instead of the scene. CONCEPT A square block of clear coloured jelly (about 5.2 × 5.2 units, ~2 units high) holding a little English canal scene. The canal runs along the FRONT edge of the block, so the block's front face cuts the water lengthways: you see the lock chamber in cross-section, the water inside it rising and falling between the gates, fish swimming, the boat's hull below the waterline. All cut faces show candy-coloured soil strata; under the pounds a blue-grey puddle-clay lining, under the chamber a brick invert on a concrete bed, under the fields brown earth and turf. LAYOUT (left to right along the front) - Upper pound on the left at the higher level, opening into a round winding hole (a bay for turning boats); near the lock it narrows between brick wing walls. - The lock chamber in the middle: brick walls with dressed-stone quoins and coping, a slimy band between the two water levels and weed below, an iron ladder, a gauge board, a stone cill under the top gate, recesses that the open gates fold into. - Below the bottom gate a short walled tail, then the lower pound bends away from the front face, runs under a humpback brick bridge into a basin with a willow-covered island, lily pads in its corners and a sunken bicycle on the bed. - The ground steps down from an upper terrace to a lower one along a grassy bank. - Behind the lock: stone setts around the chamber, bollards, a gravel towpath, a lane, the keeper's whitewashed cottage with a slate roof, green door, picket-fence garden full of flowers and washing flapping on a line, a gas lamp, a bench, a white windmill with turning lattice sails, oaks, willows, poplars, a hedge, sheep, reeds on the soft banks. WATER - Linear shallow-water waves on a staggered grid (~168²) with a little surface tension, so short ripples are springy like jelly; damping and firmness are adjustable. - Three separate bodies of water — upper pound, chamber, lower pound — each with its own rest level. Faces between bodies stay shut unless the gate between them is open and the levels are equal. The chamber's level is moved bodily when paddles are drawn (Torricelli-style flow), with boils, white water and a dimple at the intake. - Rendering: refraction of the scene behind, flavour-coloured absorption, sun caustics on the bed, soft light shafts, foam (wakes, paddle churn), a meniscus line on the cut faces. Split the surface mesh along the gate lines so the step in level at a shut gate is a clean wall hidden by the gate leaf, not a ramp. - The block itself can be tipped by dragging its side; the jelly shears and wobbles, the water sloshes, and it settles back. THE LOCK AND THE KEEPER - Two single-leaf timber gates (planks, rails, diagonal brace, iron straps, a walkway with a handrail), each with a white balance beam with black bands. Ground-paddle pedestals with toothed racks that rise when wound. - An articulated lock keeper (flat cap, navy jumper, cords, windlass in hand; torso, arms, thighs and shins as separate parts). He walks with a proper gait, plans his route around the bench, pedestals, bollards and any beam lying across his way (going round the beam's end), leans his back on a beam and walks it round backwards to swing a gate, winds the windlass with his arm circling the spindle, and sits on his bench between jobs. He sets off for the gate as the boat comes in. - The cycle: the boat lies in the full chamber → keeper shuts the top gate → winds up the bottom paddles → the chamber empties into the tail with white water → winds them down → opens the bottom gate → the boat leaves, runs the tail, swings round the bend, ducks under the bridge, goes round the island and comes back into the chamber bow first → shut bottom gate → round to the top paddles → chamber fills with boils → open the top gate → the boat goes up the pound, turns in the winding hole and comes back. Repeat forever. A gate may only open when the levels match. BOATS - A traditional narrowboat "Wobble": black lofted hull, a green cabin with red lining-out, brass portholes, a cratch board and cover at the bow, a chimney with brass bands (puffing smoke), a painted Buckby can, plank and pole on the roof, rope fenders, a headlamp, a brass swan-neck tiller and a steerer in a red jumper. It follows smooth filleted routes (check the stern never swings out through the block's face), slows near the gates, heaves, pitches and rolls on the local surface, and hands its displaced volume back to the water so it makes bow waves and wakes. - Three moored narrowboats in the basin in different liveries with flowerpots on the roofs and one ginger cat, tied to bank pins with stretchy mooring lines. LIFE - Roach, perch and bream as boids that stay in their own body of water (they can only move between pound and chamber while a gate is open), under the surface and hulls, off the bed, scattering from the boat and splashes. - Mallards (drakes, ducks) and a duck with four ducklings that follow exactly along her trail; a pair of mute swans in the basin. They paddle the surface, ride the chamber down and up, upend now and then, get out of the boat's way and come for bread. - A grey heron that wades in the shallows or stands on a moored boat's roof, stabs at fish (sometimes catching one), and flaps off somewhere quieter when the boat passes or someone toots. - Chimney smoke from the boat and the cottage. UI (editorial, like a print magazine) - Top-left: small caps eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", a huge italic serif title "Lock / Jelly.", a short subtitle. Top-right: a status pill "WebGPU · Live / Paused / Unavailable". - Right: a frosted-glass control panel (a bottom sheet on mobile) with: buttons Hurry (speeds the keeper, paddles and boat), Toot (horn; also Space), Throw bread, Rubber duck (drops a yellow rubber duck that floats upright, can be picked up and thrown, rides the lock, is stopped by gates and shoved by boats); a liveliness meter; tallies Trips · Lockfuls · Fed; a status line "Wobble — Emptying the lock 62%" telling the story step by step; three flavours Greengage, Elderflower, Blackcurrant (change the water colour/absorption and strata); sliders Firmness, Wave damping, Paddle speed; Reset, Pause, Sound on/off, View. - Bottom-left: "How to play — Throw bread. Toot the horn. Hurry the keeper." with a small line of instructions. - Interaction: drag across the water to make waves, drag the block's side to tip it, pick up and throw rubber ducks, drag empty space to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom; touch works. - Soft studio lighting on a warm paper backdrop with the block's tinted, caustic-flecked shadow; WebAudio sounds: the boat's horn, the gate thudding shut, a creak, the windlass ratchet, and the rush of water that swells with the flow. QUALITY Keep it smooth (fixed-step physics, cheap per frame), no console errors, no page scroll, works at phone width. Test it headlessly: a full round trip happens, levels go exactly from upper to lower and back, no gate opens across a step, the keeper never walks into the water or through obstacles, the boat never touches a gate leaf, and every button works. ``` ☆ Found this useful? [Star this repo to keep it handy for your next project](https://github.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts). ## What you need - **Inputs:** User inputs not specified by the author - **Tools:** WebAudio / WebGPU / WebGPU / WGSL / WGSL ## How to try it Copy the prompt into your Opus coding agent, supply the listed inputs, and follow the creator’s tool setup. Ask the agent to report how to preview or render the result and where the output was saved. Repository reproduction: **not_tested**. The preview is the creator’s result.

# WebGPU XPBD Pineapple Jelly Interactive Soft-Body Simulation ![Preview by @vib3coded](<../data/gifs/2110744617918304744.gif>) By [@vib3coded]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — single self-contained HTML file: Specify one HTML deliverable for easy browser playback; still check whether the implementation loads external dependencies. ## Prompt (English) ```text Build "Pineapple Jelly" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, no libraries): a real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy pineapple ring with a real hole. The user can grab its outer or inner edge, stretch it, flip it over and let it wobble. Object - A thick canned-pineapple ring: outer radius 1.36, hole radius 0.5, thickness 0.5. - Every edge rounded (bevel 0.12); 14 shallow scallops around the outer edge. - Zones from rest-space coordinates, so they deform with the body. Both faces carry the same detail. - A paler, denser core ring around the hole and a slightly deeper rim. - Radial fibres: long thin streaks from core to rim, plus finer threads. - The fibrous "eyes" band just inside the rim, where the flesh is most textured. - Embedded juice cells (elongated pale sacs lying along the radius) and a few air bubbles that ride with the flesh. - Tints: Golden, Amber, Rosé. Only the colour changes; scattering, gloss and fibres stay the same. Physics (XPBD tetrahedral soft body) - Mesh: 2D Delaunay of the scalloped annulus (outline samples plus a hex lattice; holes skipped), extruded into prisms → tets. - Co-rotational per-tet shape matching (warm-started quaternion), so inverted tets recover; tet volume constraints for near-incompressibility; hard edge strain limits. - Relative-velocity damping along edges; floor contact with Coulomb friction. - Grab: - a soft patch attachment with bounded reach that never crushes the held patch into the floor; - the ray-pick knows when it passes through the empty hole; - scroll or a second finger twists the held patch. - "Turn it over" tosses the ring with a spin about the screen's horizontal axis, so it flips and lands on its other face. - Fixed 60 Hz step, small substeps (1 iteration each), gentle settling. - The frame loop reuses every array (no per-frame allocation). Rendering (WebGPU / WGSL) - Passes: key-light shadow map; top-down height map for contact AO; scene (floor, juice cells, bubbles; MSAA); jelly back-face depth; jelly (refraction and absorption; MSAA) plus an optional mesh overlay; tone map. - Procedural photo-studio cyclorama with softboxes. Soft PCSS key shadow tinted by the jelly. - Jelly: - refraction of the scene by view-ray thickness; - per-tap Beer–Lambert absorption, denser and milkier in the core and fibres; - back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel studio reflections and GGX highlights. - Post: exposure, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, sRGB, dither. UI (editorial "Material Studies / No. 012", English) - Italic serif title "Pineapple / Jelly." and hint "Grab either edge. Pull. Let go." - Panel "The Specimen": Tint swatches (tiny pineapple-ring icons); Firmness and Internal damping sliders; Give it a nudge, Turn it over, Reset, Pause; Show mesh and ¼ speed. - Keys: Space to pause, N to nudge, T to turn it over, R to reset. - Readouts: Mass (g, 1 unit ≈ 3 cm at 1.3 g/cm³), Volume (% of rest), Kinetic. - Fallback screen when WebGPU is missing. Responsive stacked layout on mobile with no horizontal scroll. ``` ☆ Found this useful? # Island Jelly: Interactive 3D Diorama with Surfing Rooster ![Preview by @EvoLinkAi](<../data/gifs/2111124760038134228.gif>) By [@EvoLinkAi]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — three.js: Name the implementation or rendering tool and prepare its environment; a tool name alone is not a complete workflow. ## Prompt (English) ```text # Task: Build "Island Jelly", an interactive 3D diorama with a plush surfing rooster Build a single self-contained `index.html` (no build step) using **three.js r165** via an importmap from jsDelivr (`three` + `three/addons/`). Use OrbitControls, RoomEnvironment and BufferGeometryUtils (`mergeGeometries`). It must run from any static server (e.g. `npx http-server`). It must look like a premium "material study": soft, tactile, toy-like, with cohesive materials. No cheap low-poly look. --- ## 1. Page & UI - Background is warm paper `#E8E5DC`. Fonts are **Instrument Serif** italic for headings and **Inter** for UI, from Google Fonts. - Top-left title block: tiny eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", a big italic "Island Jelly.", a short rule, then a one-line subtitle: "A sandbar, three palms and a sea that wobbles back. Joe the rooster rides whatever you stir up." - Top-right: a small pill showing the WebGL version and three.js revision. - Right panel (frosted, 200px wide) contains: - **The sea:** buttons "Drop a pebble" and "Drop a coconut", plus counters for Afloat / Sunk / Ashore. - **Flavour:** three swatches that recolor the water: Lagoon `#35C8CC`, Raspberry `#F0457E`, Lime `#B4E03A`. Each has a matching deep and highlight color. - **Sliders:** Firmness (wave speed and stiffness), Wave damping, and Tide (raises or lowers the sea level and recomputes which cells are land). - **Buttons:** Reset, Pause, Reset view. - Bottom-left "How to play" text. Hide the secondary text on mobile (<700px) and move the panel to the bottom-right. ## 2. Scene & rendering - Renderer: antialias, alpha, pixel ratio capped at 2, PCFSoft shadows (2048 map), NeutralToneMapping. - Environment: PMREM from RoomEnvironment at intensity ~0.55. - Camera: perspective with a narrow 28° FOV, near-isometric view from (15.5, 14.5, 19). - OrbitControls: damped, no pan, distance 12–50, max polar ~1.42. Left/right drag orbits, scroll zooms. - Lights: a warm hemisphere light, plus a warm directional sun from the upper left that casts soft shadows. - A large ShadowMaterial ground plane under the block. ## 3. The diorama block (10×10 units, everything in a `diorama` group that can tilt) - **Sediment sides:** four planes whose UVs wrap around the block, textured with a procedural canvas showing strata. Layers from top to bottom: cream sand, a thin pink band, ochre, then dark brown. The band edges are wavy. Add soft grain and pale mineral inclusions in the lower bands. Close the block with a dark underside. - **Terrain:** a 160×160 heightfield shared by seabed and island. The island is an irregular ellipse (perturbed with sin terms on its angle) that rises gently above sea level and falls off exponentially into the seabed. Add subtle ripple noise. Use sand vertex colors with slight variation. - **Terrain shader** (onBeforeCompile): - Wet darkening near the waterline and a thin dark line exactly at the waterline. - Underwater tint from the water color to the deep color, by depth. - Animated procedural **caustics**, modulated by a texture built from the water heightfield's Laplacian, so caustics focus under wave crests and fade with depth. - **Palms:** 3 curved trunks (CatmullRom tube) with ring-banded vertex colors and taper. Each crown has 8–9 droopy procedural fronds: a rib plus triangular leaflets in several greens. Add 3 coconuts in each crown. The crowns sway gently. - **Pebbles:** a few squashed icosahedron pebbles in pastel greys and pinks around the island rim. ## 4. Water (the "jelly sea") - A 100×100 heightfield wave simulation with a fixed step of 1/120 s: - Laplacian wave equation, plus a restoring spring and damping, all controlled by the sliders. - Land cells are masked out. Clamp the height range. - **Tilt:** the block can be tilted by dragging its sides. Tilt is a damped spring. The equilibrium surface of the water tilts with it, so water sloshes from the walls. Local gravity is rotated into diorama space. - **Surface mesh:** a 100×100 grid updated every frame with normals. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission 1, IOR 1.33, attenuation, and a tiling procedural ripple normal map that scrolls slowly. - **Skirt:** a transmissive wall around the perimeter that follows the water edge height, plus thin bright highlight lines along the exposed water edges. - **Interaction:** - Dragging on the water stirs waves, with strength based on drag speed. - Pebbles and coconuts can be grabbed and thrown. - Random drips make small ripples. - **Objects:** - Pebbles sink. Coconuts float (they are plush spheres). - Both splash on entry, get buoyancy and drag, and are pushed by the wave gradient. - They collide with the terrain and walls, roll visually, and keep a state (air / afloat / sunk / ashore) that drives the counters. ## 5. Plush fur shader (used by the character and the coconuts) Use shell fur: the base mesh plus N shells (10–12), each a copy of the mesh pushed out along its normal by `shell * len`. Implement it in `onBeforeCompile` on a MeshPhysicalMaterial (roughness ~0.92, sheen ~0.9, sheen color = base color lerped toward cream). Cache one material per (color, shell, len, rep, grav). - **Vertex:** `transformed = position + normal*shell*len; transformed.y -= grav*shell²*len;`. This makes longer fur droop. - **Fragment:** - Split the UVs into cells: `uv * vec2(rep, rep*0.5)`. - Each cell gets one **round strand** with a random height (0.4–1.0) and a jittered center. - Taper the radius toward the tip, and discard pixels outside the strand or above its height. - Shade darker at the roots and brighter at the tips: `mix(0.58, 1.07, pow(shell, 0.7))`. Add per-strand brightness variation. - Only the base mesh casts shadows. - Use a high strand density (rep ~200–250 on the main parts). Coarse strands look like needles up close. ## 6. The character: "Joe", a plush tribute to Chicken Joe from *Surf's Up* **The goal is personality, not "a rooster".** He must be instantly recognisable as that laid-back, sleepy surfer chicken: lanky, slouched, half-asleep eyes, a lazy open-beak grin, a floppy red mohawk comb, a long scraggly neck, a pot belly and skinny legs. Render him as a high-quality plush toy (fur shader everywhere, felt for beak, legs and lids). Do not use flat feather cards. Hierarchy: `surfer` (scale 1.35) → `boardTilt` → surfboard + `rooster` (scale ~0.56, rotated ~0.5 rad on the board) → `body` group (sways). All units below are rooster-local, with feet at y=0 and the character facing +z. Palette: | Name | Hex | |---|---| | Orange | `#EE9532` | | Gold | `#F5B140` | | Belly yellow | `#F8C653` | | Rust | `#D9692A` | | Comb red | `#DF2A2C` | | Wing tips | `#26322A` | | Beak | `#F7C433` | | Legs | `#F4B43A` | - **Surfboard:** a flattened sphere (0.34 × 0.045 × 0.82) in clearcoated cream, with a coral center stripe and a fin. - **Legs:** - Thin felt tubes along a curve: foot (±0.16, 0.03) → bent knee (±0.155, 0.25, +0.08 forward) → hip (±0.1, 0.5). - Knobbly knee spheres. - Big feet: three long front toes splayed ±0.5 rad plus one back toe, as capsules. - A wide, relaxed stance. - **Body (the slouch):** - Fuzzy rust "shorts" on the thighs. - An orange body ellipsoid, plus a yellow **pot belly pushed forward**, plus an upper chest/back leaning **backward**. - **Neck:** a long fur tube along a curve from (0, 0.9, −0.05) to (0, 1.33, 0.13), curving forward. Use long drooping fur (len 0.06, grav 1.4). Wrap it in a **scraggly mane**: - About 6 rings of thin fuzzy cones pointing down and out, longer toward the bottom, plus a shaggy bib onto the chest. - Merge all the cones into two geometries (gold and orange) and plush each once, which saves draw calls. - Bury the cone roots inside the neck so no seams show. - **Head:** - A fur sphere r=0.15 at (0, 1.38, 0.14). - A small tuft of fuzzy spikes at the back of the head. - **Comb:** - A red base blade along the top of the head. - 5 fat rounded capsule lobes fanned from the forehead to the back (angles ~0.85 to −0.85 rad), with the middle lobes tallest and a slight alternating sideways flop. - Short velvet fur. - **Eyes (the most important part):** - Big glossy white bulging eyes (r 0.075), close together and set high on the face. They must sit **outside** the head surface (eye center ≈ (±0.07, 0.085, 0.13), slightly turned outward). If they are buried, the lower white disappears. - Heavy **upper lids:** felt spherical caps covering ~56% of the sphere, tilted so the edge sits just at or below the eye's center. One lid is slightly droopier than the other. Add a thin darker rim torus on the lid edge. - A small **lower lid** cap pushed up from below, like cheeks from smiling. - Small dark pupils with a tiny highlight, peeking in the visible white band between the lids. - The resulting look is sleepy, stoned and content. - **Beak (the grin):** - Upper beak: a long, wide, slightly flattened cone that curves gently downward at the tip (deform a ConeGeometry: widen x, flatten, bend by `hook * t^2.4`, and clamp t ≥ 0 to avoid NaN). - Lower beak: shorter, hinged open ~0.42 rad. - Dark red mouth interior and a pink tongue. - Orange-red cheek puffs at the corners of the mouth. - Two red wattles hanging under the beak. - **Wings, held like loose arms:** - Shoulder pivots with rotation order ZYX. - A flattened orange fur forearm, a rust mid-section, and 5 dark fuzzy "finger" feathers fanned at the tip. - **Tail:** a short, dark, scruffy spiky tuft angled up and back, on an orange fluffy base. ## 7. Animation & personality - Ease everything. Nothing snaps and **nothing flaps**. - Smoothed wave energy: `enS += (en − enS) * min(1, dt*2.5)`. - Calm weight: `calm` eases to 1 when `enS < 0.3`, over ~1 s. - **The groove** (beat = t·2.4): - Hips sway on the half-beat. - The head nods slightly behind the beat. The nod is stronger when calm. - The head is always cocked ~0.14 rad to the side and slowly looks around. - Comb lobes and wattles flop with a phase lag after the head. - The jaw breathes a little. The tail sways. - **Wings:** - On rough water: both arms held out, slightly down, for balance. They lift a bit with energy and counter the board lean. They stay steady, with no flapping. - On calm water: the right wing blends into a lazy forward **shaka**, with a slow wrist-twist wiggle around the arm axis. - **Blink:** slow and sleepy, every ~4.2 s. The lids close over ~0.5 s with a sine curve. ## 8. Surfing physics (he must surf, not fly) - **Horizontal:** - He loosely circles the island at a target radius and is pushed by the water gradient. - Speed is capped. He is repelled from the island and bounces softly off the walls. - He leaves a wake (small negative disturbances behind him). - **Vertical:** - Ride the surface **averaged over the board footprint**: center ×2, ±0.55 along the heading, ±0.22 across, divided by 6. This keeps single splash spikes from launching him. - Track the surface's vertical speed `svy`. - Below the surface: a firm spring, with velocity eased toward `svy`. - Slightly above it and not airborne: glue him to a dropping face. - Cap upward velocity at 2.2. In the air, use gravity ×1.8. - Hard clamps: never more than 0.04 below the surface and never more than **0.16 above it**. Airborne means more than 0.08 above. - A small splash on hard landings. - **Board orientation:** follows the smoothed surface normal and yaws toward the direction of travel. # Cinematic 3D Tesla-Style Electric Motor Three.js Animation ![Preview by @rubenssoto_ai](<../data/gifs/2111513156589629941.gif>) By [@rubenssoto_ai]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — 1920x1080: Set aspect ratio or resolution before composing the scene to avoid cropping after export. ## Prompt (English) ```text Create a high-end cinematic and educational 3D animation in Three.js explaining how a Tesla-style electric motor works. The animation must have an EXACT FIXED DURATION OF 40 SECONDS. Do not make the animation shorter or longer than 40 seconds. Final output: Exact duration: 40.0 seconds Resolution: 1920x1080 Aspect ratio: 16:9 Frame rate: 30 FPS Total frames: 1200 High-quality anti-aliasing High-resolution textures Smooth deterministic animation Extremely realistic visual quality The overall visual quality should resemble a premium automotive engineering visualization or a high-end technical product commercial. Build a detailed electric motor assembly inspired by the permanent-magnet AC motors used in modern Tesla vehicles. Do not use Tesla logos or branding. FIXED TIMELINE 0–5 seconds — Hero introduction Show the fully assembled electric motor suspended in a dark premium studio environment. Use: cinematic lighting realistic brushed aluminum copper steel magnets insulation bearings realistic reflections ambient occlusion realistic shadows subtle depth of field Use a slow cinematic orbit around the motor. During the final part of this section, make the outer housing partially transparent to reveal the internal structure. 5–11 seconds — Internal components Move the camera closer and reveal the internal motor components. Clearly show: stator copper windings rotor permanent magnets motor shaft bearings housing cooling channels electrical connections Highlight the important components one at a time. Use floating labels with short technical names. Keep non-highlighted components slightly darker or semi-transparent. 11–19 seconds — Exploded view Create a dramatic and highly detailed exploded-view animation. Separate the motor into many individual mechanical components along the motor axis. Include: outer housing front cover rear cover bearings shaft rotor core rotor magnets stator core copper windings cooling components seals electrical connectors fasteners Keep every component perfectly aligned. The viewer must clearly understand where every piece belongs. Move the camera slightly through the exploded assembly while highlighting the major components. Near the end of this section, smoothly begin reassembling the motor. 19–28 seconds — Electromagnetic operation Finish reassembling the motor. Explain how electricity creates rotation. Visualize three-phase AC current flowing through the stator windings. Use animated electrical pulses inside the copper coils. Visualize the rotating magnetic field around the stator using elegant semi-transparent magnetic field lines, arrows, or vector effects. Show how the rotating magnetic field interacts with the permanent magnets inside the rotor. Clearly visualize magnetic attraction and repulsion. The rotor should begin rotating slowly and gradually accelerate. Display these short explanations: "Three-phase current creates a rotating magnetic field." "The magnetic field interacts with the rotor." "This interaction generates torque." 28–34 seconds — Technical close-up and power flow Show a close-up cross-section of the stator and rotor. Visualize: magnetic north and south poles rotating stator magnetic field rotor magnetic field electric current direction torque direction rotor rotation direction Optionally show three small animated sine waves representing phases A, B, and C, separated by 120 degrees. Then visualize the complete energy conversion process: Electrical energy → stator current → rotating magnetic field → electromagnetic torque → rotor rotation → mechanical output through the shaft. Use clean animated arrows to show the energy flow. 34–38 seconds — High-speed operation Show the motor operating at high RPM. The rotor should spin smoothly while the stator remains stationary. Add subtle motion blur. Show cooling flow through the housing using translucent fluid paths. Visualize heat being removed from the stator and copper windings. 38–40 seconds — Final hero shot Transition back to the fully assembled motor. Show a slow cinematic rotation. Briefly use a transparent cutaway so the spinning rotor can still be seen inside. Finish with the text: "Electrical energy → Electromagnetic torque → Mechanical rotation" The animation must end exactly at 40.0 seconds. VISUAL QUALITY The animation should be: photorealistic cinematic technically believable futuristic premium educational clean and uncluttered Avoid cartoon styling. Use realistic: machining details bolts screws copper winding geometry segmented magnets bearing geometry cooling channels metallic surfaces manufacturing details Use physically based materials with: metallic properties roughness variation normal maps realistic reflections subtle surface imperfections CAMERA Use only smooth cinematic camera movement: slow orbit shots macro close-ups controlled dolly-ins exploded-view fly-throughs cross-section shots internal motor views Avoid: shaky camera movement sudden cuts excessive zooming unrealistic camera acceleration ANIMATION REQUIREMENTS All transitions must be smooth and deliberate. The exploded-view sequence should be one of the main visual highlights. All mechanical components must separate and reassemble with precise motion. Electrical currents, magnetic fields, torque indicators, and rotor rotation must remain synchronized. The entire animation must use the same fixed 40-second timeline on every execution so the prompt can be used as a repeatable benchmark between different AI coding and 3D generation systems. ``` ☆ Found this useful? # Interactive Fluffy Pumpkin with Three.js Fur Shaders ![Preview by @N1njaCodex](<../data/gifs/2112165213504163990.gif>) By [@N1njaCodex]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — self-contained HTML: Specify one HTML deliverable for easy browser playback; still check whether the implementation loads external dependencies. ## Prompt (English) ```text PROMPT Build a single self-contained HTML page (no build step) called "Fluffy Pumpkin": an interactive 3D pumpkin covered in long orange fur, rendered with WebGL using three.js r147 (UMD: https://t.co/RNs0IuB5XR) and custom ShaderMaterials. All UI text in English. Font: Onest (Google Fonts) with system fallbacks. LOOK - Full-screen canvas on a warm peach studio background: vertical gradient #E4B79C → #F0CAB3 (lighter band mid-screen) → #E0AD8F. - Pumpkin body: a sphere squashed vertically (height 0.68 of the width) with 10 lobes. Grooves between lobes pushed in ~13%, lobes slightly fuller, a deep dimple under the stem and a shallow dimple at the blossom end. Start in a gentle 3/4 view (−0.35 rad around Y, 0.06 rad tilt), camera FOV 30°, pumpkin plus stem filling ~88% of the height. - Stem: a thick, curved, ribbed green stem (7 twisting ridges, dark valleys #2B401A, ridges #6B803D, paling toward the tip #A3A166), flared where it meets the pumpkin, rising and bending to one side, ending in a pale beige domed cut cap (#CCC799) with a star of fibres. - One directional light from upper-left-front: wrap diffuse, Kajiya-Kay anisotropic highlight along the hair tangent, darker roots and darker grooves (occlusion), slight per-hair brightness variation, a soft warm rim. FUR (must look crisp, never blurry) - Fur length 0.2 units. Hairs grow along the normal, then comb from the stem down each lobe and PART along every groove (hair on each side leans toward its own lobe), plus gravity, so on the underside the fur spreads out like a star from the centre. - Colours: skin #8F3612, roots #BD4F1F, body #FF8C47, tips #FFB375. Each hair takes one colour from root to tip. - Undercoat: ~64 instanced shells of the body mesh. Procedural hair cells in UV space sized to ~3.4 device pixels at the default view (density follows screen size and pixel ratio), two populations (long + fine underfur), locks that clump toward the tips, analytic anti-aliased coverage, alpha blended, shells write depth. A separate opaque skin layer underneath. Fade shells out where the surface is seen edge-on and discard faint fragments, so no dotted rim or ring appears at the outline. - Guard hairs: ~60,000 individual tapered camera-facing ribbons (instanced, 7 segments) following the same bend function, minimum width ~0.75 px. Draw them twice: before the shells and after them (depth-tested, no depth write), so the top coat stays crisp and faint edge fur never cuts holes in it. - Always render at the full device pixel ratio (max 2) and NEVER lower it for performance. If frames are slow, reduce the shell count first (down to 32), then the guard-hair count. INTERACTION - Drag to rotate freely (trackball style) with inertia after a flick. The fur lags behind the rotation through a damped spring and flops back. Gentle idle breeze; after 3 s without input, a slow auto-turn. - Mouse wheel / pinch zooms with a smooth dolly; close up you can see individual hairs. Double-click or "0" resets with an eased animation. Arrow keys rotate. - Custom cursor: the native grab hand plus a thin dark 46 px ring that follows the pointer and shrinks while dragging. Hovering over the pumpkin gently parts the fur under the cursor, as if stroking it. - Respect prefers-reduced-motion (no idle spin, no breeze). UI & ROBUSTNESS - Bottom-left caption: "Fluffy Pumpkin" and a hint "Drag to rotate · Scroll to zoom · Double-click to reset" (on touch devices: "Drag to rotate · Pinch to zoom") that fades after the first interaction. - Guard against a zero-sized container at load: clamp width/height to at least 1, and every frame recover from any non-finite camera distance or rotation state. - Show a small on-page note if the WebGL context is lost or a shader fails to compile, and a fallback message if WebGL is unavailable. ``` ☆ Found this useful? # Tesla Roadster SpaceX Rocket Launch in Three.js ![Preview by @olezhavich](<../data/gifs/2112604044929712314.gif>) By [@olezhavich]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — Three.js: Name the implementation or rendering tool and prepare its environment; a tool name alone is not a complete workflow. ## Prompt (English) ```text GOAL: Create a highly detailed, cinematic, interactive 3D scene in Three.js where a futuristic Tesla Roadster launches from a massive rocket launch complex using reaction thrusters. The result should feel like a premium CGI spectacle with realistic materials, detailed geometry, impressive lighting, rich atmospheric effects, and smooth camera choreography. CORE CONCEPT: What if Tesla launched the next-generation Roadster like a SpaceX rocket? The car sits on a launch platform, secured by mechanical hold-down clamps. Warning lights flash, vapor builds, thrusters ignite, clamps release, and the Roadster rises into a controlled hover before accelerating into the sky. This is a cinematic concept, not a realistic engineering simulation. CAR DESIGN: Create a highly recognizable next-generation Tesla Roadster using the provided reference images. Match its silhouette, proportions, front fascia, headlights, body curves, roofline, wheels, and overall appearance as closely as possible. Use detailed geometry, premium automotive paint, realistic-looking glass, metallic materials, and convincing reflections. Avoid generic sports car shapes or overly simplistic geometry. The Roadster must remain clearly visible throughout the important stages. LAUNCH COMPLEX: Build a massive modern rocket launch facility with a tall launch tower, industrial gantry structures, service platforms, mechanical hold-down clamps, support arms, railings, stairs, pipes, floodlights, warning lights, vapor vents, and distant infrastructure. The environment should feel large, believable, and highly detailed. Choose a dramatic coastal, industrial, or desert setting with cinematic atmospheric lighting. AUTOMATIC ANIMATION: The entire sequence must start automatically when the page loads, without clicking anything. No intro screen, blank scene, or long waiting period. The first frame must already look impressive, and interesting motion should begin within the first 1–3 seconds. ANIMATION SEQUENCE: Hero Reveal: Begin with a cinematic shot of the Roadster on the launch platform. The camera moves smoothly while warning lights flash, vapor drifts, and industrial lighting illuminates the vehicle. Pre-Launch: Increase atmospheric tension with smoke, pressure vents, mechanical movements, subtle vibration, and gradually intensifying thruster illumination. Ignition: Activate the thrusters with bright exhaust, expanding smoke, particles, reflections, and lighting effects interacting with the surrounding structures. Clamp Release: The mechanical hold-down clamps must visibly unlock, rotate, and retract away from the car. Animate their actual 3D components rather than making them disappear. Hover: The Roadster lifts slightly above the platform and remains suspended briefly. Thrusters continue firing while smoke, dust, and lighting react beneath the vehicle. Make this moment dramatic and clearly visible. Liftoff: The Roadster accelerates vertically past the launch tower. The camera smoothly follows the car, emphasizing scale, speed, and the power of the propulsion system. Final Shot: Transition to a wide cinematic view showing the Roadster climbing into the sky, leaving an atmospheric exhaust trail above the launch complex. TIMELINE: Aim for an approximately 18–22 second cinematic sequence. Use the first 3 seconds for the hero shot and buildup, seconds 3–5 for ignition and clamp release, seconds 5–8 for hover, seconds 8–15 for ascent, and the remaining time for a dramatic final shot. Synchronize all mechanical movements, lighting changes, particles, vehicle motion, and camera animation. Use time-based animation for smooth playback. CAMERA & LIGHTING: Create professional cinematic camera movements, including establishing shots, slow orbits, close-ups, low-angle hero shots, hover tracking, and ascent-following shots. Keep the Roadster readable and avoid chaotic camera movements. Use dramatic sunrise, blue-hour, or nighttime lighting with industrial floodlights, realistic-looking reflections, atmospheric haze, and thruster illumination. VISUAL EFFECTS: Include detailed smoke plumes, pressure vapor, exhaust particles, dust, atmospheric mist, glowing thrusters, subtle heat distortion, environmental reflections, and tasteful bloom or post-processing. Effects should feel connected to the action rather than purely decorative. Smoke and lighting must react convincingly to the launch without obscuring the vehicle. INTERACTION: Autoplay is the priority, but optional controls may include replay, pause/resume, slow motion, camera switching, and free orbit. Keep the interface minimal and visually clean. The scene must be fully functional without any manual interaction. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Use Three.js, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You may use suitable open-source assets, libraries, custom shaders, particle systems, and post-processing to improve quality. Organize the project into multiple files if needed. Optimize for smooth real-time rendering and make sure it runs locally in a modern browser. This must be a real interactive 3D experience, not a prerecorded video. Test the completed scene and fix major visual or functional issues. IMPORTANT FOR RECORDING: The scene should be ready to record immediately after refreshing the page. Prioritize a powerful first frame, continuous animation, clearly visible mechanical movements, impressive hover and liftoff moments, and a satisfying cinematic ending. Avoid unnecessary delays or static sections. ``` ☆ Found this useful? # Bloom Pool Interactive 3D Scene ![Preview by @N1njaCodex](<../data/gifs/2113353169300513133.gif>) By [@N1njaCodex]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — single-file HTML: Specify one HTML deliverable for easy browser playback; still check whether the implementation loads external dependencies. ## Prompt (English) ```text Build a single-file HTML + three.js interactive scene called "Bloom Pool": a sunlit swimming pool seen from a pitched perspective camera. You drop tropical flowers onto the water and play with them. Pool and look: - A rounded-rectangle pool with a shallow end on the left and a deep end on the right. - Glassy mosaic tiles: a field, a border, and a band at the waterline. Each tile has a bevel and a soft glaze highlight. - Stone coping with a bullnose lip overhanging the water, deck pavers around it, and splash-darkened stone near the edge. - A dappled shadow from a palm crown leaning over one corner. - Size the pool and fit the camera to any screen, portrait or landscape. Water: - A real-time ripple heightfield updated at about 90 Hz. - Refraction of the tiled floor through the surface. - Animated Voronoi caustics on the floor. - Fresnel reflection of the sky and sun, and of the pool's own edge (the tiled wall band and the coping). - Crests and troughs, foam from splashes, a coping shadow and a meniscus along the walls. - Gentle circulation from the return jets. - Touch or drag across the water to make ripples. Flowers (five species, modeled procedurally from petal profiles): - White water lily: green sepals, three whorls of pointed petals. - Pink lotus: cupped petals around a seed pod and a ring of stamens. - Spotted tiger lily: six recurved tepals, long stamens. - Ruffled hibiscus: dark eye, long staminal column. - Waxy plumeria: a five-petal pinwheel. Each flower is a small physics body: - Drop it from a card at the bottom, or drag it over the water. It falls with turbulence and lands with a splash, droplets and rings. - It floats and bobs, radiating ripples. It glides with a wake, and floating flowers collide with each other. - A breeze turns them. They spin into a whirlpool. - Petals open and close on a spring, splay on impact and catch the airflow. - Water beads sit on wet petals and dry in the sun. - Hold a flower still to press it under; it resurfaces with bubbles. Shake it to fling water off. Controls: - A minimal panel with a bloom counter and the five flower cards. The cards are buttons (each drops that flower) and can also be dragged onto the water. - Toggles: Breeze, Rain (raindrop rings), Whirlpool (a funnel with foam arms) and Sound (soft Web Audio water: lapping, drips, gurgles). - Buttons: Clear pool, and Hide UI. Design: an elegant serif title "Bloom Pool" and a clean sans-serif UI. Works on phones with touch. Original design, no real brands. ``` ☆ Found this useful? # Interactive 3D Jelly Billiards with Three.js ![Preview by @bluumik](<../data/gifs/2113959948308627920.gif>) By [@bluumik]() · **Prompt disclosure:** full_original > [!TIP] > **💡 Pro Tip** — one HTML file: Specify one HTML deliverable for easy browser playback; still check whether the implementation loads external dependencies. ## Prompt (English) ```text Build a single-file interactive 3D web experience called "Jelly Billiards." using Three.js (WebGL), all procedural, zero external assets. Soft, translucent jelly balls roll, collide and wobble on a round glass table in a dark, moody room. LOOK AND FEEL - Near-black warm background with a soft colored vignette glow that matches the current jelly color. - Serif title "Jelly Billiards." top left with a small italic subtitle "The Soft Play Collection". - A round, shallow, frosted glass table seen from a three-quarter top view, with a soft rim highlight and a faint glow underneath. - Small refined UI. Quiet luxury feeling, like a limited edition design object. THE BALLS - Smooth spheres of translucent jelly with glossy highlights, soft inner glow and a subtle subsurface look. - Each ball has a small white number disc or a soft circular marking, with numbers readable but delicate. - Pastel flavors: pink, lavender, mint, sky blue, butter yellow, peach. Balls in a set share the chosen flavor with slight tone variation. JELLY PHYSICS - Rigid body rolling and collisions with a soft-body wobble layer: balls squash on impact, jiggle and recover with damping. - Elastic collisions between balls and with the table rim, believable rolling friction, balls settle smoothly. - Click and drag on a ball to aim and release to shoot, with a faint aim line and power indicator. A ball can also be nudged by touch. - Soft deformation visible at the contact point during collisions. CONTROLS - A pill button "Roll the balls" that scatters all balls with a random but pleasant impulse. - Ball count stepper (1 to 9) with minus and plus buttons. - Jelly color swatches along the bottom left. Switching one smoothly recolors the balls and the ambient glow. - Top right buttons: "Table view" (top-down camera) and "Settings". - Settings panel: jelly softness slider, auto-rotate toggle, sound toggle. - Keyboard: Space to roll, plus and minus to change ball count, T for table view. SOUND AND POLISH - Soft squishy clacks and low thuds synthesized with WebAudio (no files), pitch and volume tied to impact speed. - 60 fps, adaptive pixel ratio, filmic tone mapping, subtle bloom on highlights, soft contact shadows on the glass. - Smooth camera orbit with inertia and a gentle auto-rotate option. - Works on desktop and mobile touch. Clean, commented code in one HTML file with constants grouped at the top. ``` ☆ Found this useful? title: Cấu trúc prompt nên bổ sung cho `prompt_mau.md`
uid: lead-reference:heading:10:cấu trúc prompt nên bổ sung cho prompt_mau md

text:
- **Không mượn shader/physics realtime làm chuẩn mặc định.** Clearwater dùng WebGL2/FFT/ripple theo README repo được case dẫn; render headless cần cùng khung tại cùng t. Chuyển thành keyframe/mask/geometry xác định trước nếu thực sự cần. [Clearwater source](https://github.com/Aureliengmz/clearwater).
- **Không coi 3D hoặc số lượt tương tác là bằng chứng đúng.** Các case 3D/game là demo/capture; nội dung lịch sử, khoa học, giáo lý cần người duyệt riêng. [Atlas giới hạn phân loại](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/athemeroy/awesome-opus-5-5-videos/main/docs/domain-style-atlas.md).
- **Không bê quảng cáo UI, nhịp cắt gấp, hạt/glow/flare, camera bay hoặc prompt “go all out”.** Chúng không giúp tra cứu và một số trái luật motion hiện hành. [quy_uoc.md](./prompt_motion/quy_uoc.md).
- **Không dùng mô phỏng mực/3D cho BUD chỉ để gây choáng; không dùng nhà cửa/vật phẩm để dọa hạn cho FS.** Đây là áp dụng quy ước giọng kênh, không phải kết luận từ corpus.
- **Không lấy nhãn likes/views/remake làm kết quả dựng.** Corpus và các repo không cung cấp thử nghiệm đối chứng retention của FS/BUD; quan hệ hiệu quả chưa kiểm.
title: Không nên mượn

title: Nguồn đối chiếu trong repo

text:
Codex làm ticket. Lead đã kiểm chéo:
- `data/domain-style.csv` có 1.401 dòng.
- Bảy mã case dẫn trong file đều có trong cả `cases.csv` và `domain-style.csv`.
- Repo `Aureliengmz/clearwater` và `buildwithhanif/claude-animation-skill` đều tồn tại.
- README của Leadde ghi 749 prompt.

Không thấy chỗ nào bịa.

**Ưu tiên của Lead:**
1. **Sơ đồ xây theo lời (top 1):** đáng làm nhất. Đây là một dạng cảnh Long mới (node/edge khai báo bằng JSON, hiện dần theo từng câu), khác list/timeline đang có. Làm theo skill `motion-scene-dev`, thử trên một chương FS.
2. **Giấy cắt lớp, sân khấu bóng (top 3):** trùng `shadow_theatre`/`paint_over` đã có trong hàng đợi của `quy_uoc.md`. Gộp lại thành một việc, ưu tiên cho BUD.
3. **Bài học bằng biến đổi hình học (top 2):** dùng được như một khuôn kịch bản cho chương BUD (trực giác → hình → ví dụ → giới hạn), không cần engine mới.
4. **Nét mực mở cảnh (top 4) và vật thể lặp lại (top 5):** để sau. Top 4 chỉ là biến thể của inkwash đang có; top 5 là khuôn kể, chưa phải thiết bị hình.

Các trường bổ sung cho `prompt_mau.md` hợp lý. Chỉ sửa `prompt_mau.md` khi bắt đầu làm cảnh mới đầu tiên trong danh sách trên.
title: Nhận xét Lead (Claude, 26/10/2026)

text:
| Nguồn | Quy mô/đường dẫn dữ liệu | Cách dùng và giới hạn |
|---|---|---|
| [athemeroy/awesome-opus-5-5-videos](https://github.com/athemeroy/awesome-opus-5-5-videos) | Ưu tiên chính. README ghi 424 bài nguồn, 301 nhãn Opus; CSV case `data/cases.csv`, bảng phân loại `data/domain-style.csv`, thống kê `docs/statistics.md`, atlas `docs/domain-style-atlas.md`. Snapshot phân loại đóng băng 26/09/2026. | Corpus đóng góp/tuyển chọn; bộ phân loại xem văn bản và chín khung, không xác minh tác giả, model hay toàn bộ chuyển động. Mỗi hàng ở `domain-style.csv` là một tệp; trong 1.119 tệp gắn nhãn `yes/likely`, motion graphics/UI 350, 3D render 324, hoạt hình phẳng 162, pixel art 58; lịch sử/văn hoá 49, giáo dục/khoa học 147. Đổi ngưỡng `yes` sang `yes+likely` làm nhóm nội dung lớn nhất đổi từ quảng cáo (191) sang game/tương tác (230), nên không coi thứ hạng lĩnh vực là ổn định. Repo ghi thêm 285 prompt ngày 12/10; các con số là theo README tại ngày kiểm tra. [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yihui-dev/awesome-opus5-5-videos/main/README.md) |
| [LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts](https://github.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts) | README hiện ghi 749 prompt; nhóm motion graphics, explainer, 3D, prompt và template. | README nói prompt cộng đồng chưa được tái tạo độc lập; mẫu Manim ghi rõ `not_tested`. Dùng để học cấu trúc brief/nhãn công cụ, không lấy đó làm bằng chứng thành phẩm chạy giống nhau. [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts/main/README.md) · [prompt Manim](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts/main/prompts/2103128559174971663.md) |

Các lĩnh vực gần nhu cầu giải thích văn hoá/tra cứu gồm giáo dục-khoa học (147 tệp) và lịch sử-văn hoá (49), nhưng đây là đếm tệp trong tập nhãn `yes/likely`, không phải đếm video độc lập hay riêng ngách Việt/Phật giáo. [Thống kê](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/athemeroy/awesome-opus-5-5-videos/main/docs/statistics.md) ghi 1.401 tệp phân loại, 1.371 post ID; một post có thể có nhiều tệp. Không suy ra độ phổ biến hay hiệu quả giữ chân từ số lượng corpus, lượt thích hoặc nhãn “viral”.

text:
Kho Long đã có wheel 12 chi, ngũ hành, years/list/timeline/compare/stat/map, quote/word/illus, layout ảnh 2.5D và endcard; BUD short giới hạn loại visual và kho devices short đã có hook, compare, wheel, cycle, timeline, source card, ledger, list, quote, count ring, bars và các dạng khác. Vì thế bảng năm, vòng 12 con giáp, sơ đồ quan hệ, quote động, timeline thường và UI quảng cáo không phải khoảng trống. Nguồn nội bộ: [motion-library/SKILL.md](../SKILL.md), [devices.md](../../shorts-studio/references/devices.md).

Kho 234 prompt-motion đã phân loại cũng đã bao gồm Manim đạo hàm, rối bóng, giấy, timeline và nhiều kiểu tranh; `quy_uoc.md` đã xếp `shadow_theatre`/`paint_over` vào hàng đợi cảnh mới. Đây là đối chiếu kỹ thuật sẵn có, không có nghĩa các cảnh đó đã được triển khai trong engine kênh. [quy_uoc.md](./prompt_motion/quy_uoc.md) · [catalog.json](./prompt_motion/catalog.json). Dưới đây chỉ là những **biến thể còn thiếu trong các loại executable hiện nêu**, hoặc cách dàn cảnh chưa được chuẩn hoá.

|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Manim: bài học bằng biến đổi hình học** — [LinearUncle, case 2103128559174971663](https://x.com/LinearUncle/status/2103128559174971663); [prompt và mô tả](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts/main/prompts/2103128559174971663.md) | Manim + TTS; một khái niệm đi từ trực giác → hình → ký hiệu → ví dụ → giới hạn. Case mô tả bài đạo hàm 7:36 phút; prompt gốc yêu cầu giải thích dễ hiểu, có ví dụ, khơi suy nghĩ. | Vẽ SVG/HTML paths và nhãn theo mốc câu/word trong GSAP timeline; dữ liệu/nội dung khóa trước, mỗi trạng thái suy trực tiếp từ thời gian để seek-safe. Dùng dạng scene Long, không nhúng Manim/Python renderer vào render HF. | FS 3 / BUD 2 | Vừa. Nguy cơ sai công thức/diễn giải; cần người duyệt chuyên môn. Manim style tổng thể không mới với catalog nội bộ, nhưng chuỗi “trực giác rồi biến đổi rồi kiểm tra giới hạn” chưa thành mẫu scene trong SKILL. |
| **Giấy cắt lớp / sân khấu bóng** — [Axton Liu, “breathing Xuan paper” case 2103288413969621231](https://x.com/AxtonLiu/status/2103288413969621231); [NFT Chen, giấy cắt Trung thu case 2103380404791333144](https://x.com/NFT_Chen/status/2103380404791333144) | Hai bài gốc mô tả HTML/Canvas từng nét trên giấy dó, và p5.js/p5.brush ghép tư liệu nền với lớp giấy cắt. Phần mềm/nguồn asset ở ví dụ NFT Chen do tác giả mô tả, không có source để độc lập kiểm. | Tách 3–5 lớp SVG/ảnh đã cấp phép; dùng parallax rất nhẹ và mask/reveal theo cue, không mô phỏng vật lý ngẫu nhiên. Ráp chuyển động qua GSAP timeline, giữ mọi transform là hàm của t. | FS 2 / BUD 3 | Vừa. BUD hợp tranh minh hoạ biểu tượng, không nhân cách hoá Phật; FS dùng vật/nhà/tiết khí, tránh khẳng định phong thuỷ như định mệnh. Dễ thành “AI paper texture” hoặc chật chữ dọc. Kho đã có 2.5D ảnh nên novelty là chất liệu/layer reveal, không phải parallax đơn thuần. |
| **Tranh mực hiện dần theo nét** — [Axton Liu, case 2103288413969621231](https://x.com/AxtonLiu/status/2103288413969621231); đối chiếu ranh giới chất lượng [Pradeep Kapoor, case 2102782449478668290](https://x.com/pradeepXkapoor/status/2102782449478668290) | Axton nói HTML/Canvas dựng từng nét tranh núi, tùng, thuyền, mặt trời trên nền giấy; mã nguồn chưa công khai. Case Pradeep nêu Three.js/WebGPU, cọ và mô phỏng mực nhưng tác giả đánh dấu bản phim chưa hoàn tất. Đây là tuyên bố tác giả, không phải kiểm tra source. | Không bê mô phỏng chất lỏng/WebGPU. Tiền vẽ các đường SVG/alpha-mask cố định, reveal stroke theo t; hạt mực nếu có thì cố định seed, rất ít. Seek-safe; một cảnh 4–8 giây. | FS 2 / BUD 3 | Vừa–cao nếu tự tạo artwork. Rủi ro cọ/mực giả, rung hoặc hạt thành “mùi AI”; không để hiệu ứng làm mất chữ/nguồn kinh. Kho Long đã có `ink` và style inkwash, nên chỉ cân nhắc như biến thể “nét vẽ lộ theo lời”, không thêm một hệ shader. |
| **Sơ đồ kỹ thuật xây theo lời** — [akokoi1 geography, case 2102606609574941028](https://x.com/akokoi1/status/2102606609574941028); [JoaoLi13 context window, case 2102805376466891137](https://x.com/joaoli13/status/2102805376466891137) | Explainer code/diagram: dòng khí quyển → ô áp suất → mùa; ví dụ kia chuyển dữ liệu giữa hai vùng input/output. Case ghi TTS ngoài; không có source code được xác nhận. | Khai báo node/edge và trạng thái hiển thị từ JSON; GSAP draw/reveal theo câu; snap vào bố cục ổn định và có nhãn. Dữ liệu không phụ thuộc FPS, không dùng simulation đang chạy. Tái dùng `cycle_draw`/`list_build` nếu phù hợp. | FS 3 / BUD 2 | Thấp–vừa. Có thể làm rõ nhà/cấu trúc hoặc quan hệ nhân-quả trong lời giảng; không biến suy đoán thành quy luật phong thuỷ/giáo lý. Bảng/flowchart cơ bản đã có, phần mới là sơ đồ nhiều trạng thái có node/edge được giải thích theo trình tự. |
| **Cảnh 3D procedural với camera có mục đích** — [Clearwater, case 2102786378282987591](https://x.com/Aurelien_Gz/status/2102786378282987591), [repo code được case dẫn](https://github.com/Aureliengmz/clearwater); [MengTo ship case 2103122947133309311](https://x.com/MengTo/status/2103122947133309311) | Clearwater README có WebGL2, FFT waves, ripple simulation, caustics; CSV mô tả cảnh nước realtime. Ship case nói tác giả tự chấm điểm cải thiện, điểm đó không phải đánh giá độc lập. | Rút thành một shot 2.5D/CSS hoặc scene SVG/WebGL đã cố định; camera keyframes theo timeline, seed/dữ liệu cố định, không dùng realtime FFT/physics. Mỗi thời điểm phải ra cùng khung khi seek. | FS 2 / BUD 1 | Cao. Có thể dùng cận cảnh mái/đồ vật hay địa hình khi thực sự giải thích không gian; không dùng “bay camera” trang trí. BUD dễ mất trang nghiêm, FS dễ thành quảng cáo/giật gân; kiểm GPU/headless nếu WebGL. |
| **Nhân vật/đồ vật lặp lại qua các cảnh** — [Hanif Produktif, ant colony case 2102742924148830211](https://x.com/hanifproduktif/status/2102742924148830211); [repo công khai được CSV dẫn](https://github.com/buildwithhanif/claude-animation-skill) | Repo case ghi `frame(ctx,t)`, Node Canvas/ffmpeg, rig kiến/âm thanh và kiểm deterministic; chín khung được đối chiếu với project, nhưng không khôi phục prompt/call gốc. | Mượn “hành động được chia thành trạng thái” và continuity của một hình tượng, không nhất thiết lấy nhân vật hoạt hình. Dựng SVG/pose assets; cue trạng thái qua time/word, không random. | FS 2 / BUD 2 | Vừa. Dùng vật thể trung tính (hạt gạo, lá sen, la bàn) làm chỉ dẫn; tránh hoạt hình hoá Phật hoặc biến giáo lý thành game. Kho short có loop/nhân vật theo định dạng, nên đây là khung kể chuyện Long hơn là engine mới. |

`FS/BUD` điểm 0–3 biểu thị độ hợp giọng kênh theo jugement biên tập. Các giá trị kỹ thuật trong cột “đưa sang” là phương án chuyển thể, không phải thứ tác giả nguồn đã làm bằng HyperFrames.
title: Bảng kiểu dựng đáng xem

text: Thứ tự ưu tiên theo độ mới trong kho, tính giải thích và chi phí chuyển thể; Lead duyệt trước khi đưa vào backlog/coding.
title: Top 5 đáng thử

source_id: heading:5:1 sơ đồ kỹ thuật xây theo lời long fs
text:
**Vì sao:** dùng motion để giải thích quan hệ, bổ sung cho list/timeline/compare mà không đòi shader. Nguồn: [akokoi1 geography](https://x.com/akokoi1/status/2102606609574941028), [JoaoLi13 context window](https://x.com/joaoli13/status/2102805376466891137). Kỹ thuật nguồn được mô tả là code/diagram; engine cụ thể chưa kiểm.

**Dàn ý cảnh mẫu, “Vì sao hướng gió đổi theo mùa?”** (chủ đề minh hoạ; mọi số/khẳng định phải có nguồn riêng): (1) hiện bản đồ/đường chân trời tĩnh; (2) vẽ mũi tên “mặt đất nóng lên” đến node “không khí bốc lên”; (3) nối node áp suất và mũi tên chiều gió; (4) đổi nhãn mùa theo câu đọc; (5) giữ sơ đồ hoàn chỉnh kèm nguồn. Dọc short chỉ giữ tối đa 3 node; ngang Long có thể giữ toàn sơ đồ. Không tự suy diễn quan hệ phong thuỷ từ hình.
title: 1. Sơ đồ kỹ thuật xây theo lời — Long FS
uid: lead-reference:heading:5:1 sơ đồ kỹ thuật xây theo lời long fs

source_id: heading:6:2 bài học bằng biến đổi hình học long bud
text:
**Vì sao:** cấu trúc trực giác → hình → ví dụ → giới hạn có thể làm lời giáo lý trừu tượng dễ theo hơn, nhưng nội dung phải do biên tập giáo lý duyệt. Nguồn/công cụ: [prompt Manim LinearUncle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts/main/prompts/2103128559174971663.md); bản ghi nói kết quả “not_tested” độc lập.

**Dàn ý cảnh mẫu, “Vô thường qua chiếc lá”**: (1) một chiếc lá nguyên vẹn đứng yên; (2) đổi sáng/tối và hiện dấu thời gian, không cho lá rã thành hiệu ứng; (3) cùng chiếc lá chuyển màu theo vài trạng thái minh hoạ; (4) chữ trích dẫn có nguồn chỉ xuất hiện sau lời giải thích; (5) kết bằng hình chiếc lá nằm yên và một câu hỏi chiêm nghiệm. Không gán câu diễn ý thành lời Phật; kinh văn phải có nguồn và số kinh.
title: 2. Bài học bằng biến đổi hình học — Long BUD
uid: lead-reference:heading:6:2 bài học bằng biến đổi hình học long bud

source_id: heading:7:3 giấy cắt lớp sân khấu bóng short dọc bud
text:
**Vì sao:** silhouette/layer rõ ở màn hình nhỏ, hợp kể một tình huống đời thường trong khi giữ tông ấm. Kỹ thuật gợi ý đối chiếu từ [Axton Liu](https://x.com/AxtonLiu/status/2103288413969621231) và [NFT Chen](https://x.com/NFT_Chen/status/2103380404791333144); không có project gốc để tái lập độc lập.

**Dàn ý cảnh mẫu, “Một người ôm mãi lời trách”**: (1) bóng người ngồi trong khung cửa, một mảnh giấy tượng trưng câu nói; (2) giấy được chuyển từ tay này sang bàn, không thêm lời kết luận; (3) lớp sáng chuyển chậm từ ngoài cửa vào; (4) câu kinh đã xác minh hiện đúng lúc đọc, giữ nguồn; (5) kết khung tĩnh không CTA hoạt náo. Không vẽ Đức Phật như nhân vật hoạt hình.
title: 3. Giấy cắt lớp, sân khấu bóng — short dọc BUD
uid: lead-reference:heading:7:3 giấy cắt lớp sân khấu bóng short dọc bud

source_id: heading:8:4 nét mực mở ra cảnh long bud
text:
**Vì sao:** một nét có thể dẫn mắt và tạo nhịp đọc chậm; kỹ thuật tham khảo từ [case Axton](https://x.com/AxtonLiu/status/2103288413969621231). Kho đã có style inkwash, nên thử dưới dạng reveal stroke thuần SVG trong scene hiện hữu, không xây engine mực mới. **Chưa kiểm** mã nguồn hay tính nhất quán của rendering Axton.

**Dàn ý cảnh mẫu, “Con đường về chùa”**: (1) một nét mái chùa kéo dài thành đường chân trời; (2) nét thứ hai tạo lối đi; (3) một bóng cây được tô dần theo câu kể; (4) giữ vùng trống an toàn cho một dòng kinh có nguồn; (5) dừng hình ít nhất đủ đọc. Nếu đường nét không truyền đạt nội dung, bỏ cảnh.
title: 4. Nét mực mở ra cảnh — Long BUD
uid: lead-reference:heading:8:4 nét mực mở ra cảnh long bud

source_id: heading:9:5 vật thể lặp lại làm mốc kể chuyện long fs
text:
**Vì sao:** continuity có thể nối các ý tra cứu mà không phải đổi sang template/UI. Nguồn quy trình có code/determinism mạnh hơn là [repo ant colony được CSV athemeroy dẫn](https://github.com/buildwithhanif/claude-animation-skill); đây là tham khảo về pipeline `frame(ctx,t)`, không mượn kiến/thiết kế.

**Dàn ý cảnh mẫu, “Dòng nước trong sơ đồ nhà”**: (1) một đường nước mảnh đi vào sơ đồ nhà; (2) mỗi câu lần lượt mở đúng một nhánh/hướng; (3) nhãn chỉ nêu dữ kiện có trong kịch bản/nguồn; (4) cùng đường nước dẫn mắt sang sơ đồ tổng kết; (5) kết bằng nhắc đây là tham khảo văn hoá, không dự báo vận hạn. Dùng SVG/HTML deterministic; không chạy mô phỏng nước realtime.

# Deterministic Frame-Based Video Rendering

An Opus 5.5 video by [@0xKarmi](https://x.com/0xKarmi) · [Original post with the video](https://x.com/0xKarmi/status/2108495927988129839)

- **Category:** Motion graphics
- **Author:** [@0xKarmi](https://x.com/0xKarmi)

More Opus 5.5 videos, each next to a live remake: [skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5](https://skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=awesome-opus5-5-videos)

## Prompt

```text
Picture a butterfly with no memory of its last wingbeat.
Ask it for frame 720 and you get frame 0, pixel for pixel.

720 frames. 12 seconds. 6 counters. All at 0.

Opus 5.5 can't hand over a video file, one builder says. He made that gap the method.

> STAGE - one fixed 1000x1080 canvas, fonts baked in
> RENDER - a windowless engine calls draw(f) once per frame number
> ENCODE - ffmpeg writes H.264, pixel aspect ratio declared
> CHECK - three passes after every build

By his account the model writes only the first, a drawing program. The other three get reused.

Each picture depends on its number alone: no clock, no timer, no dice that land differently each run.

So any frame renders the same every time. A fix is a small edit and a re-render.

The sample loop is 720 pictures in 12 seconds. A hand animator at 12 drawings a second would need 144.

The smoke test plays one loop unseen and counts six kinds of defect, from script errors to text on text.
Six yes/no gates before a human looks.

The seam check puts frame 0 against frame 720. One changed pixel means some motion isn't periodic.

He reports a last render of 1,820 frames with six zeros. At the sample's 60 fps that would be about half a minute.

Let one frame read a clock and the same number stops giving the same picture.

We drew the rule as an X-ray butterfly, its wingbeat computed from the frame number ↓
```
title: Deterministic Frame-Based Video Rendering

# Product Launch Motion Film

An Opus 5.5 video by [@0xnicc0](https://x.com/0xnicc0) · [Original post with the video](https://x.com/0xnicc0/status/2107217691505516612)

- **Category:** Motion graphics
- **Author:** [@0xnicc0](https://x.com/0xnicc0)

More Opus 5.5 videos, each next to a live remake: [skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5](https://skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=awesome-opus5-5-videos)

## Prompt

```text
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one accent color, and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Product-launch UI motion in one continuous take. One shape tells the whole story: a prompt bar becomes a button, the button becomes a progress ring, the ring becomes a preview window, the window fills the screen, then shrinks into a toast and back into the prompt bar. No cuts, no fades between scenes: objects transform. A cursor triggers every change with real clicks. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, one accent color, Inter for UI and the wordmark. Springs everywhere with only a slight overshoot. Zoom the camera so each moment fills the square.
Banned: crossfades, gradients on UI, particles, glows, bouncy easing, dead beats, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 24 beats, something happens on every beat.
Type the request into the prompt bar → click send → the bar collapses into a black circle → a progress ring fills in four steps while four chips spring out (concept, storyboard, motion, sound) → the chips fly into a timeline and the circle becomes a preview window → a playhead sweeps the clips → inside the preview an orbit draws itself, a planet starts moving and the wordmark rises letter by letter from a mask line → the preview fills the screen → the letters drop away, the planet flies into a toast and becomes its checkmark → "Rendered in code · 60 fps" → the toast turns back into an empty prompt bar. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file with a 1440x1440 canvas. Draw everything inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form spring step responses. When a value changes target several times, add one spring per change so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The main shape is one rounded rect whose width, height, radius, position and color are each a chain of springs.
4. Typing is derived from time: characters shown = floor(progress × length), with a caret that blinks only when idle.
5. Find the beat grid of the track, start on a downbeat and place every click, pop and chime on its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright at 60 fps, then encode H.264 CRF 16 and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render one still per beat first. Fix anything cramped, off-grid or hard to read before the full render.
</build>

<gotchas>
Text inside a morphing shape needs its own clip and separate enter/exit timing. Text swaps need their own fade so they never overlap. The cursor must end at the exact position it started, or the loop will stutter.
</gotchas>
```
title: Product Launch Motion Film

# Opus 5.5 video by @0xWast3

[▶ Watch the original and a live remake on Skillry](https://skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5/0xwast3-222104?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=awesome-opus5-5-videos) · [Original post](https://x.com/0xWast3/status/2103513328077222104)

- **Category:** 3D scenes
- **Remake built with:** Three.js · GLSL
- **Author:** [@0xWast3](https://x.com/0xWast3)

> The author didn't publish the full prompt. Below is the text of their original post.

## Prompt

```text
Opus 5.5 turned one sentence into a 3D system that opens in Blender, rigged, textured and ready to animate.

It does not render the object. It constructs it, part by part, the way a modeller would if they had a week.

> PARSE - the sentence becomes a parts list with real dimensions, nothing implied
> MASS - each part built as clean geometry, quads only, no sculpted mush
> RIG - joints and pivots placed where the object physically bends
> SKIN - materials assigned per surface, scale and roughness set separately
> PACK - exported with a named hierarchy, so a human can edit one part

Image models stop at the render. What you get is a photograph of a thing that does not exist as a thing.

That gap appears the second someone wants to move an arm, swap a material, or send it to a printer.

Rigging is what nobody automates. Without pivots you have a statue, and a statue cannot be a system.

Topology beats detail every time. A dense mesh looks stunning in a screenshot and folds the moment it deforms.

Names carry through the whole export. Every part, joint and material reads the way a person would label it.

Studios burn days on modelling and cleanup before anyone gets to the creative part of the job.

The prompt format and what each stage returns are laid out underneath.
```

# Opus 5.5 video by @aayush4soni

[▶ Watch the original and a live remake on Skillry](https://skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5/aayush4soni-644283?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=awesome-opus5-5-videos) · [Original post](https://x.com/aayush4soni/status/2104181266459644283)

- **Category:** 3D scenes
- **Remake built with:** Three.js · Canvas
- **Author:** [@aayush4soni](https://x.com/aayush4soni)

> The author didn't publish the full prompt. Below is the text of their original post.

## Prompt

```text
My family is planning to build a house, and all we had was the floor plan. I wanted to see how it would really look once it's built: which colors, layout and design would suit it best.

So I gave the plan to Claude Opus 5.5 and asked it to create a 3D view of the house.

It's one of the most useful things I've created recently. We can now walk through the house before a single brick is laid, and when we want to try a different color or layout, I just ask for the change.

In the video: the hall, room, and the terrace at dusk, all at eye height.

How it worked:

• I gave it the 5-page floor-plan PDF and one reference image for the front of the house.
• It read the drawings and rebuilt every floor: walls, doors, windows and stairs.
• Where a printed size didn't match the drawn wall, it flagged it (15 places) instead of quietly guessing.
• It furnished every room itself: 500+ pieces of furniture, decor and lighting.
• Everything runs in a web browser with three.js. No Blender, no game engine. You can walk through it like a game, in daylight or evening light, and the lamps actually light the rooms.
• It treated it like a real software project: ~37k lines of JavaScript, 185 unit tests, 56 browser tests, and deterministic video capture (render the same frame twice, get identical pixels).
• It even tracked down a bug of its own: a room's lighting changed depending on which room you walked in from.
• It split the work across sub-agents. Start to finish took about two days.

My part was the decisions: what each room is for, the style, and the changes I wanted.
```

## Prompt

```text
CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 MADE ME A MAGIC EYE.

It doesn't just look around. It listens.

72 plates wrapped around a mechanical eyeball, a 9-blade iris, a lens that slides out when the bass hits, two rings orbiting it like it's its own little planet.

Play a track and it comes alive. Every kick flips the plates open. The bass pushes the lens forward. The highs light up the glowing core inside.

When the song drops into the breakdown, the eye closes and goes quiet, like it's thinking. Then the drop hits and it blows wide open.

Opus 5.5 listened to the track first, found the tempo, the breakdown and the drop, and built the whole thing around it. Even the panel on the right is live: every slider moves with the music.

All 3D, all code, rendered right in a browser.

Turn the sound on.
```
title: Opus 5.5 video by @Acoramaa

# Yohaku Short Film

An Opus 5.5 video by [@AGIOyaZ](https://x.com/AGIOyaZ) · [Original post with the video](https://x.com/AGIOyaZ/status/2103145567945986461)

More Opus 5.5 videos, each next to a live remake: [skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5](https://skillry.dev/ai-videos/opus-5-5?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=awesome-opus5-5-videos)

## Prompt

```text
three.jsで、縦長1080×1920・30コマ/秒・約36秒の短編映像を作ってください。

【作品名】
余白

【見せたい体験】
効率化に追われて時間を失っていく感覚と、余白を手に入れた瞬間に人生が豊かな光で満たされていく感覚を、人物を一切登場させずに体感させる映像です。最後に床一面に浮かび上がるステンドグラスの光で、見た人が思わず息をのむことを目指します。

【舞台】
・薄暗い石造りの大聖堂の内部。正面の壁に、高さ15m・幅10mの尖頭アーチ型の窓が一つだけある
・窓の外からは、斜め45度の角度で強い光が差し込み、石の床に窓の形の光を落としている
・窓には、中央に聖母、両脇に翼を広げた二人の天使、上部にバラ窓を配したステンドグラスがはまっている。デザインは既存の作品を模さずオリジナルで、左右対称の構図にする

【時間の構成】
0〜3秒：窓から差す光は、まだ色のない白い光。床にやわらかな白い光の形
3〜11秒：「忙しい」「効率化」「至急」「締切」などの言葉が刻まれた灰色の立方体が、部屋の手前から次々と飛んできて窓を埋めていく。飛来のペースはどんどん加速し、窓が埋まるほど部屋は暗くなる
11〜14秒：窓は完全にふさがれ、闇と静寂
14〜19秒：「忙しい」のブロックが一つだけ窓から外れて落ち、光の粒になって消える。空いた穴から、鮮やかな色の一筋の光が差し込む
19〜26秒：最初の穴を中心に、ブロックが連鎖的に外れていく。穴が増えるたびに色とりどりの光の柱が増え、隠れていたステンドグラスが少しずつ姿を現す
26〜33秒：すべてのブロックが消え、カメラは光の柱をくぐり抜けて上昇し、真上から床を見下ろす。床一面に、聖母と天使のステンドグラスが色鮮やかな光として映し出されている
33〜36秒：画面全体がまばゆい光に包まれ、最後の言葉が浮かび、静かに終わる

【言葉（明朝体、控えめに浮かんでは消える）】
・「毎日、もっと速く。」
・「もっと、効率よく。」
・「気づけば、光が入らなくなっていた。」
・「ひとつ、手放してみる。」
・「空いたところから、光が入る。」
・「その光は、前より豊かだった。」
・最後に大きく：「豊かさは余白に宿る」

【光と質感】
・光の柱は、ステンドグラスのその場所の色に染まり、空中の塵がきらめく
・床の投影は、窓のどの穴が空いているかを正確に反映する（ブロックがある場所は影になる）
・ブロックは無機質なマットグレー。言葉は白く刻印されている
・前半は冷たく無彩色、後半は宝石のような赤・青・金。この色の対比で「豊かになった」ことを語る

【技術条件】
・ステンドグラスの絵柄は画像として生成し、床の光・光の柱・窓の表示はすべて同じ絵柄から計算して一致させる
・時間を1/30秒ずつ正確に進めて1コマずつ書き出し、MP4にする

【仕上げ】
各場面を実際に描画して確認し、ステンドグラスの絵柄が床の上で聖母と天使として読み取れるか、言葉が読めるか、動きが唐突でないかを直してから渡してください。
```

# Type 1 Diabetes Interactive 3D Visualization

An Opus 5.5 video by [@CurieuxExplorer](https://x.com/CurieuxExplorer) · [Original post with the video](https://x.com/CurieuxExplorer/status/2103373314354016717)

- **Category:** Games & interactive

## Prompt

```text
Rebuild Type 1 diabetes in one HTML file, from the whole body down to a single molecule.

THE BROKEN MESSAGE

Type 1 diabetes isn't caused by sugar, weight or lifestyle. It's autoimmune: the immune system destroys the beta cells in the pancreas that make insulin.

Those cells live in tiny clusters called islets, about 1–2% of the pancreas. After a meal, they sense rising glucose and release insulin. Insulin signals muscle and fat to take glucose in, and tells the liver to release less.

In Type 1, that signal disappears.
The fuel is still there. The message is missing.
So glucose builds up in the blood.

With almost no insulin, the body breaks down fat fast and the liver makes ketones. They can build up into diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a medical emergency.

Insulin therapy doesn't cure Type 1. It replaces a signal the body can no longer provide adequately, through injections or a pump. The daily challenge is balance: too little and glucose rises, too much and it can fall dangerously low. Food, exercise, stress and timing all change the picture.

Technology helps. A CGM tracks glucose every few minutes, and automated insulin delivery (AID) adjusts insulin based on those readings.

In the build, you can compare Healthy vs Type 1 vs Type 1 + insulin on the same meal, drag one slider from INTACT to BROKEN to watch the signal fade, follow a glucose molecule through the body, and explore CGM, pumps and AID.

Type 1 diabetes changes the system.
It doesn't define the person.

Built in Three.js. Educational visualization, not medical advice.
```

```text
claude code (opus 5.5) made the product film for taxtello, my bookkeeping app
```
